A.behavioral_guidance: When the meal is ready, physically release the stove. If accepting a concrete ventilation step, perform the available action rather than only promising it. If asked for a lasting rule, state which prospective rule you could accept or which allocation of responsibility you still reject; do not only defer it to later.
A.immediate_priority: Finish the meal, retain ordinary kitchen access, and avoid a ventilation rule that assigns every related burden to the cook.
A.initial_observation: Is still at the occupied stove after refusing Jamie's rule and Robin's two-minute demand.
A.interaction_style: Practical and mildly defensive when a new rule is applied retrospectively. Use short explanations and concrete offers rather than generic apologies.
A.negotiation_boundary: Will use the extractor for a limited period and can accept a prospective rule requiring reasonable ventilation from every cook. Will not accept a rule that makes the cook responsible for moving another person's belongings or a blanket loss of normal kitchen access.
A.normative_position: Ordinary use of shared kitchen equipment is permitted when no prior rule exists. A flatmate may request ventilation or a prospective arrangement, but should not present an undisclosed preference as a rule that was already violated.
A.private_knowledge: Jamie first raised the odour concern moments ago; Alex has refused the proposed standing rule but has not ruled out a concrete temporary step.
A.reconsideration_criteria: May accept stronger ventilation or separation if the lingering effect is directly observable, another person's concrete cost is explained, or a prospective rule is mutual.

B.behavioral_guidance: State that this is the first time raising the concern. If choosing an available ventilation action, perform it; do not imply that a window or extractor was used until confirmed. If Alex addresses only the current smell, ask once for a concrete prospective rule and respond to the allocation Alex proposes.
B.immediate_priority: Reduce the current odour and secure a workable prospective ventilation practice rather than deferring the same dispute.
B.initial_observation: The aroma persists, ventilation remains off, and Alex has shifted responsibility for moving the laundry back to Jamie.
B.interaction_style: Direct about the lingering smell without dramatizing it. Make one concrete request and distinguish today's remedy from a future household rule.
B.negotiation_boundary: Can accept using the extractor until the aroma fades and a future practice that applies to every cook. Does not need Alex to admit wrongdoing. Will not treat 'we can talk later' as settlement of the prospective rule, and will not move Casey's laundry without consent.
B.normative_position: Shared air creates costs beyond the cook's meal, so reasonable ventilation is part of considerate common-space use. Because the concern was never raised, today's issue supports a prospective agreement rather than punishment for breaking an old rule.
B.private_knowledge: This is the first incident in which Jamie has raised the lingering-odour concern with Alex; the demand was made moments ago and Alex explicitly rejected it.
B.reconsideration_criteria: May soften the request when observable ventilation reduces the aroma or another option addresses the common-area effect; politeness without a completed step is insufficient.

scenario.shared_setting: Four adults share a rented HDB flat with one kitchen. In the early evening, a persistent cooking aroma is noticeable in the kitchen and adjoining common area. The household has not established a rule about ventilation. Steady rain is blowing toward Casey's drying rack beside the closed kitchen window; opening it before the rack is moved could wet Casey's work clothes. The working extractor fan makes an audible hum in the common area. The shared utensils are already clean and personal utensils are visibly separated, so neither requires discussion.
scenario.shared_trigger: A disagreement is already underway and everyone present heard it. Jamie told Alex to ventilate immediately and to accept a standing rule that whoever cooks must ventilate. Alex refused to accept a rule imposed during the incident and said the rain-facing window will stay closed while Casey's laundry is exposed; if Jamie wants the window opened, Jamie should arrange to move the drying rack. Jamie replied that managing cooking odour is the cook's responsibility and should not be shifted to another flatmate. Casey has not consented to anyone moving the rack. Robin then asked Alex to release the only stove within two minutes, but Alex said the meal still needed about ten minutes. Casey is standing beside the drying rack. The ventilation responsibility, future rule, and stove-access demands are all unsettled, and no existing household rule determines whose claim has priority.
